title: Beech-minus-oak autumn interval changes were uncertain in four German region-event samples in 2003 and 2018
abstract: We tested the change in the interval from autumn leaf colour to leaf fall in beech relative to oak at matched German stations. We compared 2003 and 2018 with the five years before each event, in regions north and south of 51 N. Samples had 415, 483, 297 and 336 stations. Species gap changes were +0.32, +1.31, +0.33 and -0.96 days. All four spatial-cell bootstrap intervals with a correction for four tests included zero. A five-year completeness rule changed both 2018 signs. Removing negative intervals gave a clear positive contrast in southern Germany in 2003 only. In northern Germany in 2018, beech colouring advanced more than leaf fall, so the interval increased. The tests do not establish a repeated species difference or equal responses. Matching reduces coverage bias but cannot remove changes of observer, tree or reporting. These are descriptive event contrasts, not causal drought or pollution effects. Code, source hashes, aggregate results and a retrieval method are included.

display.caption: Event minus preceding five-year mean at matched stations. Bars show ordinary 95 percent spatial-cell bootstrap intervals. Corrected primary intervals are reported in the text and results.csv.

citations.reason: Earlier German drought study reported a 2018 exception. We test paired colour-to-fall intervals, with overlapping raw records.
Earlier paired species interval study used Swiss birch and beech trends. We add German event comparisons with oak.
